entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tiberius Claudius Severus Proculus was a Roman Senator born in the 1st century AD, tracing his lineage through his mother to Emperor Marcus Aurelius.


This prominent Roman Senator played a limited role in dynastic politics, but his family's influence and connections to powerful figures of the time cannot be overstated.




Proculus's significance lies in his association with the imperial family and the broader Roman elite, providing valuable insights into the inner workings of the Roman Senate during the late Republic and early Empire.










Tiberius Claudius Severus Proculus was a key figure in the complex web of Roman politics during the 1st century AD, reflecting the intricate dynamics of imperial succession and senatorial influence.
